### Exact predictive and betting results

Lower log loss, Brier score, and ECE are better; higher accuracy is better.

| Period / arm | Fights | Log loss | Brier | ECE, 10 bins | Accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2025 validation — v7 | 398 | 0.6078343126229621 | 0.2091795084301225 | 0.0736785140767535 | 0.6809045226130653 |
| 2025 validation — control | 398 | 0.6083831162697709 | 0.20948731968259937 | 0.06248106792914071 | 0.6809045226130653 |
| 2026 fixed held-out test — v7 | 224 | 0.5880418804641874 | 0.2003090125165694 | 0.055175911946618084 | 0.7142857142857143 |
| 2026 fixed held-out test — control | 224 | 0.5864636778047168 | 0.19939601364766268 | 0.07166165433573377 | 0.7321428571428571 |

On validation, v7 was fractionally better: the candidate-minus-control differences were `-0.0005488036468088708` log loss and `-0.0003078112524768639` Brier; accuracy tied and v7 had worse ECE. Those validation differences were not statistically resolved: log-loss 95% bootstrap interval `[-0.003991266701721626, 0.0027178455265976682]`, `p=0.3805`; Brier interval `[-0.0018194025416646727, 0.0011180480686965707]`, `p=0.3435`; McNemar `p=0.6170750774519739`, with two uniquely correct fights per arm. On the fixed held-out 2026 test, v7 was worse by `0.0015782026594706178` log loss and `0.0009129988689067225` Brier, made four fewer correct picks, and had better ECE. The test differences were also not statistically resolved: the log-loss difference's 95% bootstrap interval was `[-0.014365572760851788, 0.019505250883301125]` with `p=0.558`; the Brier interval was `[-0.006254045501661086, 0.008784936615023812]` with `p=0.5789`; and McNemar's accuracy test was `p=0.3427817111479112` with seven control-only correct fights and three v7-only correct fights.

On the 111 fixed held-out test fights with verified T-1 prices, the market baseline had log loss `0.5236785865891331`, Brier `0.17174181974367142`, ECE `0.11692965573944997`, and accuracy `0.7567567567567568`. On those same rows, v7 had log loss `0.5303800871497663`, Brier `0.17473218556582504`, ECE `0.08445064521565648`, and accuracy `0.7567567567567568`; the control had log loss `0.5383387472319584`, Brier `0.1776205547834616`, ECE `0.08145032704334851`, and accuracy `0.7747747747747747`. The market was the best probability baseline by log loss and Brier.

The fixed realistic betting simulation on those same 111 priced test fights used a $500 starting bankroll, 2% edge threshold, quarter-Kelly sizing, 4% cap, and the frozen realistic execution rules. Every attempted v7 and control bet filled; neither arm had a liquidity or cash skip. It produced:

| Arm | Bets | Wins | Wagered | Profit | ROI | Max drawdown | Final bankroll | Average CLV |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| V7 | 67 | 49 | $1,297.09 | $146.75998753165032 | 0.113145570108204 | 0.26706791819419645 | $646.7599875316505 | -0.001544191508606795 |
| Control | 59 | 39 | $1,039.34 | $127.10423664705387 | 0.12229322132031277 | 0.2655648339367966 | $627.1042366470541 | -0.0003495061006327097 |

V7 therefore earned `$19.65575088459645` more simulated absolute profit, but its ROI was `0.00914765121210877` lower, its maximum drawdown was `0.00150308425739984` worse, and it placed more bets and risked more total money. This is useful evidence, not a promise of future profit.

The favorable part of v7's predictive comparison was concentrated in rows where its method data was incomplete, but that slice did not create a positive overall test improvement. On 176 v7-method-complete test rows, v7/control log loss was `0.5861373761023225` / `0.5798966342477088`; on the 48 partial-or-empty rows it was `0.5950250631243581` / `0.6105428375137462`. The fixed dependency flag was therefore `false` because the total test log-loss result still slightly favored the control.

### Owner decision

**OWNER DECISION / AUTHORIZATION:** After reviewing that v7 was slightly worse than the control on the aggregate fixed held-out 2026 prediction metrics, the owner selected v7 to become the main production model. The owner accepts that measured tradeoff because the control is built on prepared data with known quality and completeness problems, especially in recent method-history and moneyline coverage, while v7 is built from the corrected, fully documented data and showed strong performance with small differences that were not statistically resolved, substantially better recent feature coverage, full moneyline coverage, and more simulated absolute profit.

This is a deliberate owner judgment about trustworthy data and maintainability; it is not a claim that v7 clearly beat the control statistically, beat the market baseline, or had higher simulated ROI. It also records approval to perform a controlled manual promotion in the next dedicated session, not a claim that promotion or deployment already happened.

## Historical identity-repair truth — 2026-08-22 checkpoint

The material below preserves the earlier identity-repair checkpoint. The approved v7 state above supersedes its old next-action language.

The Jean Silva problem was real and was not limited to one displayed value.

Two UFCStats fighters share the name Jean Silva:

- older Jean Silva: UFCStats ID `9211aae062b799d6`, born in 1977;
- current featherweight Jean Silva: UFCStats ID `52ef95b5860fb28c`, born in 1996.

The old pipeline joined some histories and profiles by name. It gave the modern Jean Silva the older fighter's birthday and 2005 fight history. That contaminated age, experience, rolling form, career counts, and related opponent-history features.

The normal checked-in `data/processed/features.csv` is still the old unscoped snapshot. It has 9,667 feature rows for 9,338 fights and lacks `fighter_a_id` / `fighter_b_id`; the normal checked-in `fights_cleaned.csv` also lacks those ID columns. The semantic publication guard therefore rejects both files before its later Jean/sentinel checks can run. Exact-day legacy replay passes because it reads stored event-day values directly, while prefight reconstruction fails on 19 of the deterministic 25 sampled fights because the old files cannot represent identity-scoped rolling history.

The independently repaired source is currently uncommitted in the portable sibling worktree, and a corrected isolated dataset plus full-fit models were generated outside the repository. The corrected snapshot separates both Jean Silvas and shows the modern fighter at plausible modern ages. It contains 9,338 fights and exactly 9,338 feature rows.

This was a class of name-collision bugs, not a single Jean Silva typo. Eleven known canonical-name collision groups were identified. The repair process inspected 112 historical rows and protects other duplicate names such as Bruno Silva, Mike Davis, and Victor Valenzuela.

The 2026-08-22 independent audit follow-up verified every F1–F9 claim before changing code. It confirmed the important defects but corrected several audit claims: the alias regression count was 421 rather than 426, 83 rather than 84 active official names were affected, the blanket supplement-quarantine diagnosis was too broad, and several example aliases did not reproduce. Corrections were kept narrow. The existing production alias design—curated aliases plus roster-derived official/UFCStats/profile/slug aliases—was inspected read-only and preserved rather than rebuilt globally.

The isolated corrected candidate is green:

- exact parity: 250 fights, 211/211 features, zero mismatches and zero build failures;
- prefight parity: 250 fights, 211/211 features, zero forbidden mismatches and zero build failures; all 2,491 differing values were in the ten explicitly allowed time-aging fields;
- scheduled quality gate: `HEALTHY` on 1,761 evaluation fights and 10 folds;
- full-fit refit: completed successfully for all three model artifacts; and
- no canonical data/model file, production manifest, Railway setting, deployment, or live-betting state was changed.

The old-default parity failure must remain visible until migration. Do not remove, blanket-skip, xfail, or routinely ignore the test. `data/processed` is a real fallback for local CLI and evaluation paths, not just a disposable fixture. Do not overwrite only the two CSVs: processed-data hashes, models, training spec/provenance, bundle fingerprints, and rollback identity must move together.

The move from 211 fields to 205 fields was separate. The 205-field contract was created by removing exactly the following six fields after an overly strict recent-data gate:

- `a_ko_odds_prob`
- `a_sub_odds_prob`
- `a_dec_odds_prob`
- `b_ko_odds_prob`
- `b_sub_odds_prob`
- `b_dec_odds_prob`

No other model field distinguishes the 205- and 211-field contracts. The six fields were not removed because they were proven useless. They were removed because the old gate demanded a level of timing and source proof that the owner no longer wants to use as a practical blocker.

The other 205 fields are the current working baseline. They are sufficiently populated for this work, but they are not claimed to be perfect or complete. Legitimate missing history for debutants, short-career fighters, or rates with no valid denominator must remain missing.

That document contains detailed no-fabrication and collection rules. This living handoff controls the order and scope of the reset.

## Non-negotiable data rules

1. Never make up, estimate, interpolate, complement, or default a missing value.
2. Never turn missing data into zero.
3. Never infer method odds from the result, finish method, fighter statistics, moneyline, the other five method values, or a model.
4. Exact mathematical conversion of a real posted price into implied probability is allowed.
5. A genuine historical market value may be used when its exact observation time is unknown. Label the timing honestly instead of inventing a timestamp.
6. Partial rows are allowed. Unavailable cells remain `NaN`.
7. Stable fighter IDs take priority over name-only matching.
8. Fighter A/B orientation must be checked and corrected before side-specific data is used.
9. A training row may use only information available before that fight. Current fighter records must not be copied backward into historical fights.
10. Pre-2022 bouts may supply prior career history for a 2022-or-later fight, but they may not become model-training targets under this reset.

## Anti-overengineering and anti-detour rules

These rules are binding because earlier work drifted far beyond the original data problem.

- Work on one numbered phase at a time.
- Prefer the smallest change that completes the current phase.
- Do not create another audit framework, attempt-ID system, remote anchor, hash mesh, permission ledger, frozen-control hierarchy, or one-use experiment protocol.
- Do not reopen a general audit of all 211 fields.
- Do not require perfect coverage or perfect historical timestamps.
- Do not repeat provider licensing research unless a specific purchase or account decision actually requires it.
- Do not start new calibration, noise, feature-selection, strategy, or model-family experiments before the direct v7 training/evaluation is complete.
- Do not build a database, identity service, or new platform when versioned CSV/JSON files and the existing pipeline are sufficient.
- Add only focused tests that protect the data repair, replenishment, or direct comparison.
- Do not add hundreds of governance tests around a small data change.
- If a new issue does not block the current phase, record it in the parking lot and continue.
- A useful imperfect dataset with honest missing values is better than a permanently unfinished forensic audit.
- Stop and ask the owner before materially expanding the six-step plan.

2. Do not move the primary repository directory.
3. Do not reset, clean, restore, or use a stash as the main backup.

   - copies of the untracked handoffs and method-odds evidence;

   Exclude secrets, environment files, credentials, betting ledgers, logs, and model binaries unless the owner separately places a specific item in scope. Never print secret values while building the inventory.
5. Create a clean sibling worktree and a dedicated reset branch from local commit `48ec21f884e7fb34200c5ebdc2d708bb56dd1482`, not blindly from `origin/main`.
6. Seed required ignored/untracked inputs into the new workspace as immutable, hash-checked inputs. Do not overwrite the originals.

### Required actions

2. Keep the two Jean Silvas separate by UFCStats ID.
3. Resolve all known duplicate-name groups by stable ID or leave ambiguous rows unresolved and excluded rather than guessing.
4. Preserve fighter IDs in processed fight and feature outputs.
5. Correct reversed A/B side-specific odds and statistics.
6. Ensure missing statistics remain `NaN` and observed zero remains zero.
7. Ensure unknown title-bout, empty-arena, and scheduled-round values remain unknown rather than guessed.

9. Build into a new versioned output directory first. Do not overwrite canonical files until checks pass.

- No duplicate canonical fight keys exist in the intended training universe.
- Reversed source rows swap every paired A/B field consistently.
- Rebuilding twice from the same inputs produces the same rows and values.

### Completion evidence

- Before/after Jean Silva examples.
- Collision-group reconciliation report.
- Focused identity, orientation, missing-value, and rebuild tests.

## Phase 3 — Use 2022-present fights as model examples

### Goal

Make the owner's desired training universe explicit without erasing useful earlier career history.

### Required rule

- Model example or target row: `event_date >= 2022-01-01`.
- Prior-history input: any legitimate fight before the target fight, including pre-2022 fights.
- A pre-2022 fight may affect a 2022 fighter's prior record, rolling history, experience, and style features, but it is not itself a training, validation, or test example.
- A later fight may never affect an earlier row.
- Build chronological prior-only features from the full legitimate history first, then filter the finished target rows to 2022 onward. Do not filter the source history to 2022 first.

### Required actions

1. Add one explicit, tested configuration or dataset contract for the 2022-present target universe.
2. Rebuild features chronologically using all legitimate earlier history.
3. Publish separate counts for:
   - all UFC source fights;
   - 2022-present fight rows;
   - completed and labeled 2022-present model rows;
   - excluded or unresolved rows and reasons.
4. Produce a simple feature-missingness report. Do not turn ordinary structural missingness into a new recovery campaign.

### Completion evidence

- Exact target-row rule and counts.
- Chronology test proving future fights do not affect earlier features.
- Test proving an experienced fighter entering 2022 retains legitimate pre-2022 history.
- Versioned 2022-present modeling dataset hash.

Recompute these counts on the identity-correct Phase 3 dataset before recovery. Do not assume the denominators remain identical after correction.

### Required actions

1. Reconcile the main historical archive, unmerged local snapshots, and recovery evidence before collecting anything new.
2. Prioritize March 2026 through the present, then earlier partial and empty rows from 2022-2025.
3. Search practical lawful sources thoroughly and record successes and failures in a resumable work queue.
4. Store real raw prices or source probabilities and per-cell provenance.
5. Allow honest historical timing categories, including `historical_market_timing_unknown`.
6. Keep partial real rows and leave unrecovered cells `NaN`.
7. Preserve conflicting observations and select deterministically. Do not silently average them into a made-up canonical value.

### Completion condition

Phase 4 does not require 100% coverage. It is complete when:

- all existing local sources have been reconciled;
- every missing fight has been attempted through the practical source list or has a recorded reason further work needs money, credentials, or owner action;
- every accepted value traces to a real observation;
- no value was estimated or invented; and
- exact remaining gaps are reported by year and field.

## Phase 5 — Establish reliable future collection

### Goal

Prevent the same data gap from growing again.

### Approved schedule for this implementation

- Tuesday at 11:00 a.m. `America/New_York`: one combined Roster Watch membership-snapshot/delta, official upcoming-event safety-net, fighter/profile, completed-fight/result, detailed-statistics, staged-build, coverage, and publication-safety run.
- Wednesday at the same Eastern time: retry the full data update only if Tuesday's data update failed. If Tuesday's accepted data succeeded but that month's candidate failed, retry only the candidate.
- A successful Tuesday prevents a duplicate Wednesday data run. If both data attempts fail, preserve the accepted generation and wait until the next Tuesday.
- Durable state survives service restarts and prevents duplicate weekly imports or duplicate completed monthly candidates.
- Replace the current daily full refresh only after local and hosted checks pass and the owner separately authorizes the Railway schedule change.
- Existing odds/live/betting cadences are outside this narrow schedule change and must remain unchanged.

### Collector requirements

- Idempotent repeat runs.
- Immutable raw snapshots for new observations.
- UTC retrieval time and scheduled start when available.
- Stable event, fight, and fighter identities.
- Explicit handling of replacements, cancellations, postponements, and A/B reversals.
- Retries for temporary failures.
- A visible warning when parsing unexpectedly returns zero or coverage drops sharply.
- Permanent finalized training observations rather than only a short-lived cache.
- Missing remains missing when collection fails.

Start with the existing collector and refresh machinery. Extend it narrowly. Do not build a new platform unless the existing code cannot meet one of these requirements.

Build and test the schedule locally. Do not deploy or activate a hosted schedule without separate owner approval.

## Phase 6 historical benchmark — completed V7 training and evaluation

### Completed goal

One reproducible candidate was trained from the approved v7 table and evaluated honestly against the current control before the owner made the promotion decision.

### Comparison contract used

The owner's direction superseded the earlier plan to begin with a new 205-versus-211 sweep. The completed run did not reopen feature, noise, calibration, strategy, or hyperparameter experiments.

1. Verified the v7 hash and reran the already-passing prepared-feature preflight.
2. Froze the existing chronological evaluation contract before fitting.
3. Trained v7 with `full_live_contract_v6_durability_fullfit` and retained its reproducibility metadata and artifact hashes.
4. Evaluated the v7 candidate and current control on the same eligible evaluation fights and shared executable betting assumptions while preserving each model's pinned feature contract.
5. Reported the result and stopped for owner approval without automatic promotion or deployment. The owner later supplied that explicit approval.

The run kept fixed wherever the contracts permitted:

- the same fixed chronological evaluation periods;
- the same model family and hyperparameters;
- the same seeds;
- the same missing-value behavior;
- the same calibration;
- the same prediction and betting rules;
- the same executable-price assumptions; and
- the same metrics.

The existing locked chronological evaluation contract was recorded before fitting. Because the full-fit training spec had no embedded test rows, the run used the existing external evaluation/backtest contract instead of inventing or tuning a split after seeing results.

The completed report records at minimum:

- number of fights in each split;
- field coverage in each split;
- log loss, Brier score, calibration, and accuracy;
- realistic number of bets, profit, ROI, and drawdown;
- performance by year;
- artifact/data hashes and the exact rows used; and
- whether any result depends mainly on rows with missing method data.

It also includes the plainly defined T-1 market baseline so model accuracy is not mistaken for a betting advantage.

The comparison itself did not automatically authorize production promotion, deployment, or live betting. The owner subsequently reviewed the result and explicitly selected v7 for controlled manual promotion; that later decision is recorded in the current-state section above.

## Owner-approved safeguards before V8 training and promotion review

V7 training and evaluation are complete benchmark evidence. The safeguards are implemented and focused-tested locally, the targeted 92-cell follow-up and identity-validator hardening are complete, exact `u30h1` has been accepted atomically, and the first bounded repeat-blocker remediation is complete. Publication-disabled r5 preserved accepted data and proved the 19-fight / 72-statistics append, but it is blocked by newly exposed Daria/Anderson lifecycle, Delphine decision, and non-source-limited identity coverage. A separately authorized remediation, another publication-disabled candidate, separate review of any clean accepted update, a true no-change repeat, Sunday/Tapology and monthly-job testing, the complete suite, and hosted checks remain. The owner requires the intended promoted model to be newly trained and evaluated from frozen V8; neither V7 nor a future V8 candidate may be promoted or deployed automatically.

### Unusual fight results

- Store the official raw result for every fight, including disqualification, draw, and no contest.
- Do not force a draw or no contest into the binary Fighter A/Fighter B training target. Keep the row for history, but exclude it from binary winner-model training.
- Store a disqualification as the official result, but exclude it from winner-model training by default unless a later, tested contract explicitly supports it.
- Flag or quarantine unusual outcomes so a refresh never crashes and never silently invents an A/B winner.
- Keep sportsbook or market settlement rules separate from model grading; settle a bet according to that market's official rules.
- Apply these rules only to new incoming fights. Do not rewrite or retrain v7.

### Scheduled refresh and retraining

Do not assume the existing jobs are fixed. The active local implementation must audit the roster update, completed-fight/data refresh, candidate-only monthly path, and proposed Railway schedule, commands, environment, paths, and logs.

Use the smallest practical approach:

1. Test each job thoroughly and immediately on local data. Manually invoke it, simulate repeated runs and calendar boundaries, and exercise missing, malformed, partial, and temporary-failure cases instead of waiting days or months.
2. Make the validation gate deterministic and fail closed. It should check the exact schema, prevent unexpected historical-row changes, allow only approved appends/corrections, reject duplicate fight identities, validate required fields and ranges, and explicitly handle normal/DQ/draw/no-contest outcomes.
3. If any check fails, preserve the last accepted dataset and model, block refresh/training/promotion, and produce one short reason or alert. Do not auto-repair uncertain data.
4. After schedule deployment is separately authorized, run one controlled hosted smoke test to verify the actual Railway schedule, command, environment, paths, and permissions; there is no need to wait for the real weekly or monthly trigger.
5. Keep every model promotion manual. The monthly job may build a candidate and evaluation report only after the first successful weekly update of a UTC month; it must never replace the production model, and its first recurring run is the month after the owner-approved V8-based model is promoted and stable and after separate activation permission.

Gemini or another LLM cross-check is deferred to the back burner. Deterministic checks come first. If revisited later, it should be advisory only and must never write data or promote a model automatically; a cloud API could run while the local computer is off.

## Post-`u31r1` track — Automatic mapping and enrichment of new Roster Watch fighters (owner decisions 2026-09-03; recorded at round-4 checkpoint C, NOT implemented)

This section records a NEW track that starts only after `u31r1` finishes (checkpoint C, and D if the owner schedules it). It was copied at round-4 checkpoint C from `C:/Temp/u31r1/OWNER_DECISIONS_AUTOMATIC_MAPPING_2026-09-03.md` (7,461 bytes / SHA-256 `da59a6547fca41d96c389e25fa4d16b5c37e9834b4cae59ae7396e6b1b7857f3`). The text below is that file's content from its `Facts established` heading to its end, byte-for-byte, with each `##` heading demoted to `###` so the track stays one handoff section. Nothing here authorizes implementation inside the `u31r1` checkpoints, nothing here changes the `u31r1` rules, prohibitions or evidence, and nothing of it was implemented at checkpoint C: the five pending additions of 2026-09-03 were not bound, and the fail-closed-on-any-addition gate is unchanged on disk. Implementation happens in its own later session under its own brief, with the same network rules, and with the gate change and the M-error change reviewed read-only before any wire use.

### Facts established from the code before the decisions (portable worktree, uncommitted)

- The adapter `src/data/rosterwatch_active_roster.py` records a Roster Watch addition with no carrier as
  `pending_external_carrier` under a provisional owner id. Binding it to a UFCStats id happens ONLY through a
  hand-written record in the reviewed-additions evidence table (status `bound`, owner decision, pinned capture
  hashes). There is no automatic lookup.
- `scripts/run_scheduled_ufc_refresh.py` fails closed: with any unresolved carrier (or sync not complete) it raises
  before the event safety net and before any enrichment, so nothing publishes. Checkpoint B showed this on real
  data: five additions between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-03 made recurring-01 production_ready false.
- Roster Watch columns used today: `fighter` and `date_of_birth` only (plus `next_date` / `next_opp` inside the
  reviewed evidence records). The record columns (`bouts`, `wins`, `losses`, `streak`, ...) are parsed into the raw
  snapshot and used nowhere. Fight counts and records seen by the model and the betting rules come from the
  project's own UFCStats-derived fight history (`a_num_fights` / `b_num_fights`).
- Betting rules: S (Single) and C (Conviction) require `MIN_FIGHTER_FIGHTS = 2` per fighter; C also skips when
  the count is unavailable. M (Model Tracker, `find_flat_model_bets`) has NO experience gate; its only skips are
  missing event time, event already started, the betting window, and missing model probabilities. The live
  data-quality gate in `src/bot.py` withholds fights upstream of all traders.
- The bot activity monitor (`/api/bot-activity`) is fed by bot.log WARNING/ERROR lines plus runtime component
  issues; M's decisions go only to the tracker decision JSONL and never appear on the activity feed as errors.
- None of the Roster Watch code is deployed: the primary worktree has no roster.watch references; the adapter is
  untracked and the scheduler changes are uncommitted in the portable worktree.

### Decisions (owner, 2026-09-03)

1. Build an automatic mapping feature. When Roster Watch adds a fighter with no carrier, the bot adds them, fills
   in what public sources have, and keeps upgrading the record on every weekly run as more data appears. Fully
   automatic. "Correctly" means never wrong, sometimes incomplete: the bot waits rather than guesses.
2. Roster Watch is trusted 100% for membership and for every field it publishes. No separate confirmation of a
   fighter's existence or membership is wanted. The only remaining check is that the page found on another site
   (UFCStats, UFC.com, Tapology, Sherdog) is THIS fighter's page: exact name plus matching date of birth, with
   Roster Watch's name and DOB as the truth. A name alone never binds (August-2026 audit P0 stands).
3. Exception to (2): Roster Watch's fighter RECORD may be wrong. It is the one field to cross-check, and only
   softly: a mismatch between the record on a linked page and Roster Watch's record is flagged for a look, never
   used to reject or accept a link on its own. (It is not used anywhere today; keep it out of features.)
4. Replace the fail-closed-on-any-addition gate without letting easy data go unimported. Two dials:
   - Effort stays at maximum: every unconfirmed fighter is re-checked against every source on every run, within a
     bounded request cap (politeness and block avoidance: UFCStats challenge pages, Sherdog Cloudflare, Roster
     Watch's default-UA block). If the cap binds, rotate oldest-first so everyone is re-checked within a few runs.
   - Blocking loosens only for unbooked additions: a pending member is carried (materialized, `coverage_eligible`
     false) and the refresh publishes. Hard stop remains when Roster Watch shows a fighter as booked (`next_date`
     set) and the bot still has no confirmed link: the data is then both available and needed.
   - Expose pending counts and aging every run: pending, newly confirmed, pending longer than N weeks, and
     "pending but a UFCStats page exists" (must be zero; otherwise a defect that turns the run yellow).
   - Turn checkpoint B's sealed captures (five additions, six event cards) into permanent regression tests.
5. The weekly re-check is plain scheduled code (HTTP fetch, parse, exact compare, write with evidence). No
   language model anywhere in the decision path. At most an LLM may draft a review note for a tricky case, and
   even that is deferred; start with none.
6. Bring in Tapology and Sherdog as extra sources for new fighters, after the two official sites work. Each needs
   its own identity link under the same exact name + DOB rule. Their main value is pre-UFC history for the tiered
   debutant rule (major / feeder / regional org tier), plus height and reach.
7. A fight with an unconfirmed fighter is skipped. S and C already skip via the two-fight rule (an unconfirmed
   fighter shows zero UFC fights). Add an explicit "identity unconfirmed, skip" for M.
8. Activity monitor: when M purposely skips a fight for an ACTIONABLE reason (unconfirmed fighter, fighter history
   unavailable, model probabilities missing, withheld by the data-quality gate), it must appear on the bot activity
   monitor as an ERROR naming the fight, the fighter, the reason, and what clears it; deduplicated through the
   alert-store fingerprints, with a recovery when the fight is bet or the fighter is linked. Timing skips (event
   started, outside the window, no event time) stay ordinary activity. Applies to M ONLY; S and C skipping an
   inexperienced fighter is the strategy working as designed. Because the data-quality gate withholds fights before
   any trader sees them, the M error must also be raised at that withholding point.
9. Standing rules may retire categories of manual decisions (e.g. DOB disagreement with an exact name and exact
   bout match: trust Roster Watch's DOB, accept the link, flag). Cases no rule covers wait for more evidence; they
   never guess. A review list exists for the owner to look at when they want, not one that must be cleared before
   the bot runs.

### Expected double signal (by design)

A booked, still-unlinked fighter surfaces twice: early from the weekly refresh hard stop (data side) and late from
M's skip error (betting side). Same root cause, one fix (link the fighter). Both are honest; neither is a bug.

# Appended u45a1 local implementation and measurement checkpoint

# Local native custody and saved-helper connection - u45a1

September 6, 2026. The remaining local controller, retained-head recovery, native custody and saved-helper connections are implemented and tested. The workflow remains disabled and uninstalled. This is a local implementation checkpoint, not completed computer-off hosted operation.

## What is implemented

The connected controller now consumes checkpoint callback returns and independently confirms the exact requested original, retained accounting head and current retention head before continuing. Recovery asks the independent custodian for its current checkpoint; it rejects an older supplied head. Merely passing the historical preservation callback still grants no independent custody.

Native provisioning requires fresh, already immutable root-owned accepted trees, trusted ancestry, a different controller UID and no existing process with that UID. It preserves intended inventory modes and exact bytes. The root-owned controls bind the accepted pointer and release, complete owner/membership dependencies, initial checkpoint, policy and saved-response fixture. Historical source-plan references inside captured envelopes are preserved as inert provenance; they are not relocated, reconstructed or treated as executable inputs. Named policy/fixture substitutions are rejected even when the substitute has identical bytes at a different path.

An independent root service keeps the latest retained head and a chained intent/commit journal. Each connected store mutation obtains durable external intent before its local writes, and an exact committed acknowledgment before returning. Source claim markers and result body/raw/envelope blobs are inside that boundary. An outstanding uncommitted intent blocks fresh recovery, preserving uncertainty and consumed IDs. No automatic tail adoption, refund, retry or repair is provided. The legacy unguarded store path retains its previous behavior and carries no new independent-custody claim.

The saved-response helper runs separately, checks the exact claimed plan/review and pending charge, and requires the independently committed current charge head. It saves and fsyncs a one-use response record before returning bytes. The controller communicates over preopened anonymous pipes after the existing native socket/process guard is installed. The new explicit CLI obtains starting inputs and named controls from custody, exposes no production clock override and preserves real calendar refusal. Live roster/fighter egress is not implemented or authorized by this saved-only connection.

## Restart continuity and interruption behavior

`scripts/roster_local_continuity.py` now constructs and returns a v2 read-only
continuity observation; the caller saves the record outside the native tree.
It observes a canonical native boot identity around supplied clock readings,
requires nondecreasing UTC observations during capture and on verification,
and retains exact file, native identity, ownership, mode and independently
current head checks. A boot mismatch fails before the supplied clock or
semantic capture is used. A v1 record lacks the new clock observations and is
rejected for continuation; it remains evidence. No old record is repinned.

This detects an observed boot change or observed backwards clock movement. It
does not establish trustworthy elapsed time, clock rate, suspend behavior or
downtime. A passing byte comparison and matching point timestamps cannot supply
crossboot accounting authority. The fresh native tests simulate changed boot
markers through controlled observations; they do not claim an actual machine
reboot or successful reboot recovery.

The saved restart design identifies the missing independent evidence: a
still-valid external witness session/epoch, a fresh challenge tied to the new
boot, exact current custody/accounting/retention state, and a justified UTC
uncertainty interval evaluated in full against the original lifetimes,
deadlines, calendar and budgets. Existing point-clock interfaces cannot safely
choose a favorable endpoint from an uncertain interval. No such witness,
clock bridge or crossboot recovery API was implemented or claimed.

Recovery still requires the exact latest independently acknowledged retained
checkpoint. It can legitimately be an ancestor of newer independently
committed accounting. Checkpoint lag alone establishes neither refusal nor
successful recovery. Full ancestry, independent evidence, uncertainty,
original lifetimes and consumed-plan checks remain mandatory. Uncommitted
intents, unanchored tails, rollback and mismatches with the independently
committed head fail closed. No generic crash reconciliation, refund, silent
resend, archived-state restoration or consumed-plan reconstruction was added.

Thirteen new restart cases and 24 new interruption cases were added. They cover
